questions.prompt: In `EVAL script numkeys ...`, what does numkeys tell Redis?

options.text: How many times to run the script
How many of the following arguments are keys (populating KEYS), with the rest going to ARGV
The maximum runtime in milliseconds
The number of return values

questions.explanation: numkeys splits the arguments: the first numkeys of them are key names (KEYS[1..]), and the remainder are ARGV. Passing keys explicitly is also what lets Cluster route correctly.

questions.prompt: Why must Lua scripts be kept short and fast?

options.text: Because Lua is a slow language
Because a script runs atomically on the single command thread, blocking all other clients while it runs
Because scripts can only use 1 KB of memory
Because EVAL charges per second

questions.explanation: A script's atomicity comes from monopolizing the one command thread, so a long-running script freezes every other client until it finishes.

questions.prompt: Which statements are true? Select all that apply.

options.text: A Lua script executes atomically — no other command interleaves
EVALSHA runs a script cached by its SHA-1 hash
Redis Functions are persisted with the dataset and replicated
EVAL scripts are permanently stored in RDB/AOF like data

questions.explanation: Scripts are atomic, EVALSHA uses the cached SHA-1, and Functions are persisted/replicated. EVAL scripts are only an ephemeral cache — they are NOT stored with the dataset.

questions.prompt: What is a key advantage of Redis Functions over EVAL scripts?

options.text: They run faster because they skip atomicity
They are named, loaded as a library, and persisted/replicated with the data
They can block the server without consequences
They do not need keys or arguments

questions.explanation: Functions (Redis 7.0+) are first-class: named, managed as a library, and stored with the dataset (RDB/AOF) and replicated — unlike the ephemeral script cache behind EVAL.

questions.prompt: Inside a Lua script, you invoke a Redis command with redis.____('SET', KEYS[1], ARGV[1]). (the function name that raises on error)
questions.explanation: redis.call runs a command and raises an error (aborting the script) if it fails; redis.pcall instead returns the error as a value.

questions.prompt: Why should a script receive the keys it touches through KEYS rather than hard-coding them?

options.text: It makes the script run twice as fast
So Redis knows which keys are accessed, which is required for correct routing in Redis Cluster
Hard-coded keys are not allowed in Lua
It reduces the SHA-1 length

questions.explanation: Declaring keys via KEYS lets Redis (and Cluster) know which keys the script operates on, which is necessary to route the command to the right shard.
